pr_title: [browser] Fix fingerprinting of relinked dotnet.js during build
pr_body:
- dotnet.js from runtime pack is replaced by relinked version
- reading `NuGetPackageVersion` metadata doesn't produce a value
- instead we read the version from runtime pack file and than pass it to the task

Depends on https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/85730
Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/30802
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86959

@radical, what's the error string here? to unblock current PRs

> @radical, what's the error string here? to unblock current PRs

`Could not find blazor's dotnet*js .*_framework` - I have updated the known-build-error json too.

review_comments: Do we need it to be this specific? The regex that I had pushed should capture the version, and hash without being specific about the format.

Sorry, I override it by accident. 

Anyway, since we are checking whether the file is fingerprinted as expected, the more strict the regex is the better, isn't it?

This is the regex I was suggesting: `@"\.(?<version>.+)\.(?<hash>[a-zA-Z0-9]+)\.` .
- it assumes the format for the hash, and combined with the `".js"`, it makes up the end of the string, and thus can be matched easily
- And we know the prefix, like `dotnet.native.`, which allows the remaining part to be extracted as the version.
- We can then check the version if we want, but even if we don't it doesn't depend on the format of the version string. A stricter *version* regex would be more fragile.
Ook, I'll revert to your suggestion 👍
